seo.title: Why BFS Always Finds The Shortest Path
seo.hook: The first time breadth-first search reaches a station, that is already the fastest way the
seo.description: You can find a shortest path without comparing any paths, because the order of exploration does it for you.

scenes.narration: The first time breadth-first search reaches a station, that is already the fastest way there. Always.

scenes.headline: Everything [one stop away]
scenes.caption: the first ring
scenes.narration: |Now the neighbours. A connects to B and to C. |For each one we ask whether we've seen it before, and neither of them has been. |So we mark them visited, |and push them onto the back of the queue, each carrying zero plus one, which is one stop. ^B goes on. ^C goes on. +The queue now holds B and C, +both at distance one. That's the first ring of the ripple, and nothing at distance two can be looked at until both of these have been.

lines.detail: Look at everything this station connects to.
Mark it, so nobody queues it again.
Push it on the BACK, one stop further out.

scenes.premise: A subway map. Each circle is a station, each line a direct connection, and the badge on a station is how many stops it sits from A.

scenes.headline: Why [visited] matters
scenes.caption: C finds D already taken
scenes.narration: |Now C comes off the front, ^also one stop out, and it isn't our destination either. C connects to D as well, and here the code does something that looks like nothing. |D is %already in the visited set, so we skip it. Without that skip D gets queued twice, and on a map with a loop the search never finishes.

lines.detail: Already visited, so skip it. This is the guard.

scenes.premise: A subway map. Each circle is a station, each line a direct connection, and the badge on a station is how many stops it sits from A.

scenes.headline: Arrived, in [three stops]
scenes.caption: the answer
scenes.narration: |E comes off the front, ^three stops out. Every station nearer than three has already been taken off and dealt with, |so when we ask whether E is our destination, and it is, we return the distance it carried: %three. We compared no routes at all, because the first arrival is the shortest arrival.

lines.detail: Arrived. Return the distance it carried.
